the regional blood flow is an important determinant of the rate and degree of lignocaine penetration into the blood stream, and therefore of its systemic absorption and pharmacokinetics.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the current dosage recommendation for local anaesthetic administration should not be applied indiscriminately, but that it should be modified in respect to the regional blood flow at the site of administration.
the current dosage of lignocaine used for infiltration anaesthesia is probably too small and should be modified in relation to the regional blood flow at the site of injection.
